content.confidence: 3: You are fairly confident in your assessment. It is possible that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work. Math/other details were not carefully checked.
content.summary_of_the_paper:
The paper proposes a new time-series forecasting architecture called Focal Decomposed Network (FDNet). The network is simple and effective. It consists of only CNN and MLP, but yields very promising results on popular deep time-series forecasting datasets. The main design principle of FDNet is: 
  1. split the input sequence into 4-5 chunks with an exponential difference in size. The closer the chunk is to the prediction time, the shorter the chunk.
  2. train 2D CNN to denoise input chunks independently, the closer the chunk to prediction time, the more complex the denoising filter
  3. map directly the denoised chunks into the output sequence using independent fully connected layers, then add up the result.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
  - The proposed FDNet and its "focal input sequence decomposition" component is simple yet effective. Empirical results are strong.
  - The alternative FUNet design is also interesting with good empirical results.

Weaknesses:
  - The definition of "Input Correlation Oriented Mechanism", or ICOM, is unclear and not very useful to me. The paper claims that most forecasting methods rely on extracting (auto-)correlation within input sequences to form global features before forecasting. This is only an artifact of imposing some inductive biases. The earliest application of Neural Net on forecasting tasks was simply training MLP to predict the future sequence from multiple lag variables. In some sense, I find FDNet fairly similar to that approach.
  - From my understanding, in the FDNet design, the CNN component plays the role of learnable denoising filters, while most of the forecasting power is in the FC layers. The output prediction is basically the sum of different FC outputs, each taking different denoised lag sequences as input. Therefore, most learnable params are in FC layers. However, the paper does not describe FC layers in detail. An analysis of learnable params per component would be very appreciated. That would also show how the learnable params scale when the input length increases.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The paper is well presented with high-quality figures. I find them very useful to understand the model architecture.
The architecture proposed in the paper is conceptually simple and easy to re-implement. Its empirical performance on the popular time-series dataset is very promising.
content.summary_of_the_review: The FDNet proposed in the paper is simple yet empirically effective. The paper is well presented with good experiment setups.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper presents a time series forecasting method that less relies on the commonly adopted paradigm of temporal dependency, which is named input correlation oriented mechanisms (ICOM) in this paper. The proposed method considers the past time series as decomposed subsequences, and designs networks based on convolutional structures, making predictions mostly rely on most recent subsequences. The experiments aim to demonstrate without ICOM, time series forecasting could be improved using the proposed method.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength
1. The paper provides a summary of many time series forecasting method, and found a commonly used paradigm, which may not be indispensable.
2. The paper provides a discussion that aims to justify the feasibility of excluding ICOM and using decomposed input for forecasting.
3. The paper introduces one possible method follows its motivation that address ICOM.

Weakness
1. Many conclusions in this paper are not well justified. For example, the paper claims time series forecasting task tends to pursue connections of previous and future sequence instead of only the correlation of previous sequences. This should be proved or validated. It is obscure on how to use future sequences for forecasting. Similarly, it claims many forecasting methods including transformers have performance drops and parameter explosion when dealing with prolong sequences. This should be further elaborated for being convincing.
2. The paper claims the forecasting task without ICOM is still valid by only doing the projection of input sequence to the prediction sequence. This is infeasible if the length of the prediction sequence is unknown and variable.
3. The paper aims to show ICOM is not indispensable in Section 2. However, the proof is too descriptive to be solid. It is hard to evaluate how the conclusion at the end of Section 2 was reached and justified by its aforementioned descriptions. A formal proof or a comprehensive experimental study (comparison of different methods on different datasets with valid metrics).
4. The paper uses many terminologies, which seem to be new, e.g., ICOM, LSTI, TSFTs, network expression skills, universal feature map, etc. Some of them are not easy to understand and make the paper difficult to follow.
5. The introduction of the proposed method is also too descriptive. It is better to use mathematical formulations when appropriate to make the description more accurate. The reason of some design choices of the proposed method are unclear, e.g, why to choose convolutional structures, why to use 3x1 Conv in Fig 4, and how are the proportions 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/8 in Fig 5 where determined. The method design lacks solid theoretical support.
6. The proposed method learns features from each variable of the time series. This may overlooks the correlation between different variables when learning features.
7. In the experiments, it is better to include confidence interval in the tables to demonstrate the statistical difference between different methods.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper aims to show without relying on a widely used assumption in time series forecasting, the performance is still good or could be improved. It introduces a method with such design, and validate it with experiments. The paper is not well written, some conclusions are not well justified. The method design is not sufficiently clear. See details in strength and weakness.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
The paper addresses the time series forecasting problem.
The authors propose a model that learns a latent representation
of each channel in isolation through MLPs and convolutions
(with shared parameters) and then forecasts the output via
a fully connected layer. In experiments they show that their
model outperforms several baseline models.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
s1. very simple model with some plausible inductive bias.
s2. experimental results look promising.

w1. experiments miss three typical datasets, a closely related baseline and
  some details.
w2. the concept of "input correlation oriented mechanisms (ICOM)" is not really clear.
w3. the claimed relation to distribution shift is not really clear.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The writing of the paper could be improved, esp. explaining and delineating
more clearly the concepts ICOM and the relation to distribution shift.
The proposed architecture is composed of standard layers, but the very
assembling is novel.
Reprodicibility is medium (experiments are explained clearly, but no code is
provided).
content.summary_of_the_review:
I see three issues:
w1. experiments miss three typical datasets, a closely related baseline and
  some details.

  Most papers also compare on the datasets ETTh2, ETTm1 and ILI. Why did you
  omit them?

  The DLinear model by Zeng et al. 2022 proposes an even simpler model with
  comparable results to yours. What advantages does your model have?

  The results in tab. 2+3 are hard to read, as
  a. they do not show standard deviations, so one does not know which differences
     might by significant, which are just random.
  b. showing MSE and MAE side-by-side makes it hard to compare models.
  c. highlighting the 2nd best model would help readers even further to read the table.

w2. the concept of "input correlation oriented mechanisms (ICOM)" is not really clear.

  First I thought you wanted to propose a single channel forecasting model, that
  just shares parameters across channels. But then in fig. 3 you put a fully connected
  layer between the last latent layer and the output. Is this really full connected?
  Or fully connected per channel, sharing parameters? If it is fully connected,
  then also your model learns from other channels, it just correlates them in the
  last latent layer. So what does ICOM really mean?

  At the end of section 2 you claim, that your analysis shows that "having no ICOM"
  is "feasible, general, robust and practical", but I do not see how your analysis
  is showing that. 

w3. the claimed relation to distribution shift is not really clear.
  

references:
  Ailing Zeng, Muxi Chen, Lei Zhang, Qiang Xu:
  Are Transformers Effective for Time Series Forecasting? CoRR abs/2205.13504 (2022)
